identity.name: Fedbank Financial Services Limited
identity.industry: Diversified NBFC — Gold Loans + LAP (secured retail lending); Federal Bank subsidiary

summary.oneLiner: the near-term noise is optical, reported gold-loan overdues will look elevated as customers transition from bullet to periodic-interest structures, but this is "customer behaviour in transition, not an asset-quality concern" given highly realizable collateral.

one-line thesis: A consistency quarter for the Federal Bank-backed secured NBFC: AUM +35% YoY to Rs 21,136 cr and PAT +52.5% to Rs 114.4 cr, with ROE crossing the psychological 15% (15.4%, +380 bps YoY) and ROA 2.6% — even while absorbing a Rs 13 cr negative direct-assignment hit (deliberate DA wind-down) and a mid-quarter RBI gold-LTV regime change. The twin engines (gold + LAP) are intact; the near-term noise is optical — reported gold-loan overdues will look elevated as customers transition from bullet to periodic-interest structures, but this is "customer behaviour in transition, not an asset-quality concern" given highly realizable collateral.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Adjustments: negative DA income of Rs 13 cr (deliberate DA reduction) suppresses headline NII/net income. GNPA aided by ~Rs 51 cr write-off (board policy) — normative GNPA ~1.87% (flat vs March). Leverage rose 4.6 → 4.89x as transition issues pushed would-be co-lending (CLM) business onto own balance sheet. Stage 2 up 2.2% → 2.7% — entirely the gold bullet→periodic-interest re-adjustment.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Gold AUM growth 25-30% FY27 (on flat gold prices) — via tonnage growth (10-12%) + LTV expansion on quarterly/half-yearly products.
Entity AUM growth ~20-22% FY27; Mortgage / LAP AUM 15-20% FY27 (medium-ticket + small-ticket).
ROA expansion 20-30 bps over FY26 average (~2.4%) → via credit-cost + cost-to-avg-assets levers.
200 branch additions in FY27 (none opened in Q1 — premises identified, spillover into Q2; 150 added last year).
Gold tonnage growth 10-12% FY27 (Q1/Q2 seasonally soft, H2 picks up).
De-leverage over next few quarters as CLM/co-lending normalizes (from 4.89x); adding co-lending/DA partners to conserve capital.
Gold mix expected to rise a few points toward ~54% of book if gold outgrows LAP.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business — pipeline = disbursement momentum + branch expansion. Q1 disbursements Rs 6,760 cr (+14%). 200 branches identified but unopened (Q2 spillover). Present in ~18 states; Odisha flagged as a wide-open expansion territory plus north in-territory density. Gold AUM/branch Rs 17.7 cr; ~400-500 gold-only branches where ST LAP is not yet cross-sold (the unification-of-command synergy lever). Auctions this quarter negligible (<Rs 1 cr).
segment / subsidiary detail: Gold Loans: AUM Rs 11,191 cr (+77% YoY, 51.4% of book); LTV 67.9% (up from 61% on gold-price fall, on-boarding LTV unchanged); tonnage +1% QoQ (+8.1% QoQ AUM despite ~15% domestic gold price fall Jan-Jun + Apr-1 regime change). Lends on lower of 30-day avg or spot. Doorstep Gold Rs 1,787 cr (+96.5%). IGL (income-generating) product to compete with banks on higher-LTV.

Mortgages: AUM Rs 9,777 cr (+14%); Medium-ticket LAP (Rs 35 lakh-3 cr, yield ~12-12.5%, Tier 1/2, competitive yield pressure) + Small-ticket LAP (Rs 7-35 lakh, yield ~16%, Tier 3/4). Disbursals held back on yield/approval-rate discipline ("growth is an outcome"). Old ST-LAP book behaving as guided; new book better delinquencies.

Co-lending (CLM) / DA: transition issues under new gold rules pushed CLM onto own book (leverage 4.89x); Rs 589 cr LAP + ~Rs 300 cr gold DA done; DA income deliberately negative (unwinding > new booking).

Leadership: George Oommen joins as Business Head – Gold Loans (30+ yrs, under Jagadeesh Rao); Shardul Kadam → Chief Transformation Officer; Jagadeesh Rao takes additional charge of ST LAP + Home Loans (branch as the "epicentre").
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Gold + ST-LAP branch unification — ~400-500 gold-only branches to cross-sell ST LAP (shared target market, distribution, geographies) under Jagadeesh Rao. 2) IGL / quarterly-monthly gold products — regulatory-driven product innovation (higher LTV on serviced loans). 3) Doorstep Gold (+96.5%). 4) Geographic expansion (Odisha + 200 branches). 5) Co-lending scale-up with more partners (capital-light growth).
margins & cost dynamics: Yield (ex-DA) +10 bps QoQ to 15.7% despite tanked-up liquidity (Gulf-geopolitics hedge) that kept incremental borrowing costs +20-30 bps over Q4; weighted-average CoB still fell 3 bps QoQ. Rate outlook benign on FCNRB flows in Q2. Cost-to-income improved >400 bps QoQ to 52.8% — primarily core-income expansion, aided by Q1 seasonally-low sourcing (expected to rise as originations pick up). Opex/avg total assets 4.8% (-70 bps), creating room to invest in 200 new branches while sustaining ROA. LAP yield under competitive pressure (~12-12.5% medium-ticket); FEDFINA holding yields rather than chasing disbursal.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Branch-led: 200 branches planned FY27 (0 opened Q1 — premises/investment done, Q2 spillover; 150 added FY26). Branch remains the growth epicentre (3-4 year vision). No large physical capex beyond branch build-out.
capital allocation: CRAR 20.71% (from 22.4%) — dip partly from CLM shrinkage onto balance sheet. Strategy: conserve capital by routing incremental AUM through CLM/DA partners (de-lever from 4.89x). ~Rs 51 cr deeper-bucket NPA write-offs per board policy. True North (long-standing PE holder) fully exited 6.86% (25.7M shares) via block deal → acquired by Nomura India Equity Fund (FPI) — a shareholder-register change, not company capital.
risks & watch-items: 1) Gold regime optics — reported 1+/30+ DPD and Stage 2 (2.2→2.7%) elevated as bullet→periodic-interest transitions; management says optical/auction-backed, not asset risk. 2) Gold price — 15% fall Jan-Jun; further falls compress LTV/AUM growth. 3) Leverage at 4.89x until CLM normalizes. 4) LAP yield competition (medium-ticket) — disbursal held for quality. 5) Monsoon / West-Asia macro — no stress seen yet, possible Q2-Q3. 6) Mortgage Stage-3 — lengthy SARFAESI enforcement; collections team beefed up, "long haul".
management quality / tone: Parvez Mulla measured and consistent — "same set of priorities for five quarters, unchanged": secured book, gold+LAP twin engines, DA reduction, sub-1% credit cost. Candid that disbursal is deliberately an "outcome" (yield/quality first), that gold overdues will look optically worse, and that branch openings slipped to Q2. CFO C.V. Ganesh precise on DA accounting, FVOCI reclassification and the write-off math. Reiterated all FY27 guidances "intact." Tone: rebuild-credibility, under-promise/over-deliver.
non-obvious takeaways: The 52% PAT growth is core-income, not DA — FEDFINA is deliberately shrinking DA income (negative Rs 13 cr) and still grew net income 33% and PPOP 50%; the DA wind-down is a self-inflicted headwind that makes the core trajectory cleaner going forward.

The gold regime change is a reported-delinquency reset, not a credit event — entire bullet book moved to interest-due; a single missed interest now reports the whole loan overdue, so 1+/30+/Stage-2 optics rise sector-wide with unchanged auction economics.
Leverage spike (4.6→4.89x) is a CLM plumbing issue — would-be co-lending sat on own balance sheet during the transition; de-leverage as partners re-onboard is a coming ROE tailwind.
Branch unification (gold + ST-LAP) is the quiet operating-leverage lever — 400-500 gold branches with no ST-LAP = latent cross-sell on shared distribution/target-market.

PAT Rs 114.4 cr (+52.5%), ROE 15.4% (+380 bps), ROA 2.6%, EPS >Rs 3. GNPA 1.6% (-30 bps, ~Rs 51 cr write-off; normative 1.87%), NNPA <1.0%, PCR 38.36%, credit cost 0.8%. Yield ex-DA 15.7% (+10 bps), CoB -3 bps, C-I 52.8% (from 57.2%), opex/assets 4.8%, CRAR 20.71%, leverage 4.89x. Negative DA Rs 13 cr; Stage 2 2.2→2.7% (gold regime). True North exited 6.86% → Nomura India Equity Fund. Q2 FY27 → check: (1) do gold 1+/30+/Stage-2 optics stabilize under periodic-interest? (2) leverage de-levering from 4.89x as CLM normalizes; (3) 200-branch openings landing (Q2 spillover); (4) gold tonnage picking up H2; (5) LAP yield vs disbursal trade-off; (6) credit cost holding sub-1%; (7) FCNRB-led CoB relief.
